DNDAMIGOS.Menu.Title: D&D Amigos
DNDAMIGOS.Help.Title: How to Use This Module
DNDAMIGOS.Help.Sync.Title: D&D Amigos Sync (on each character's sheet)
DNDAMIGOS.Help.Sync.Body: On any PF2e character's sheet, click D&D Amigos Sync in the header. If the actor isn't linked to a Character Vault entry yet, pick one to pull its stats onto this actor, or create a new entry from this actor's current data. Once linked, clicking it again lets you choose Pull from Site (overwrite this actor with the site's data) or Push to Site (overwrite the site with this actor's current stats and portrait) — a campaign's DM can push for any character in it, not just their own.
DNDAMIGOS.Help.PostEvent.Title: Post Session Update
DNDAMIGOS.Help.PostEvent.Body: Sends a short message to the campaign's Discord, with the option to also log it as a real entry in the site's session log.
DNDAMIGOS.Help.ManageLoot.Title: Manage Loot (the Party Stash)
DNDAMIGOS.Help.ManageLoot.Body: Party loot lives in Foundry now: the PF2e Party actor's inventory is the party stash. Drag items in from compendiums or character sheets, split coins and hand things out there, all standard PF2e. Manage Loot opens a small Party Stash window: coins and item count at a glance, Open Party Inventory, and Sync Loot to Site, which sends the stash to the website's Party Loot page (anyone can sync, whenever you like; the site only shows a read-only snapshot). Unidentified items go up under the name you see, without level or value. The first time, the GM can also Import Site Loot to bring the old site-side ledger into the stash.
DNDAMIGOS.Help.Lookup.Title: NPCs & Places
DNDAMIGOS.Help.Lookup.Body: Search the campaign's NPCs and Places, open one to read it, and add notes the whole party can see. Notes are shared with the website: anything you write here shows up there and the other way round. You can edit or delete your own notes (the DM can delete anyone's). You need to set your identity first (My D&D Amigos Identity) so your notes are credited to you.
DNDAMIGOS.Help.ImportInfo.Title: Import from D&D Amigos (GM only)
DNDAMIGOS.Help.ImportInfo.Body: Pulls the campaign's Places and NPCs into this world as Journal Entries, and shows your E.Y.F.F.O. mini-game stats in a popup if you've set your identity and played it.
DNDAMIGOS.Help.Identity.Title: Your Identity (personal token)
DNDAMIGOS.Help.Identity.Body: End of Session Sync, character syncs, NPC & Place notes, Post Session Update and the E.Y.F.F.O. stats popup need to know which D&D Amigos member you are. On the website, open your Account page and use Foundry Connection → Create token, then in Foundry open Configure Settings → My D&D Amigos Identity, paste it, press Check, and Save. It's saved in this browser only, so do it once on each device. Treat it like a password; if it ever leaks, Replace it on the Account page.

DNDAMIGOS.Help.PushLore.Title: Push NPCs & Places to Site (GM only)
DNDAMIGOS.Help.PushLore.Body: NPCs and Places are written here, in Foundry, as pages in the "D&D Amigos: NPCs" and "D&D Amigos: Places" journals. Start a page with an italic line (the tagline), then the description. This button sends every page up to the site and remembers which is which, so pushing again updates the entry instead of duplicating it. A picture on the page becomes the portrait. The site shows plain text, so formatting is flattened. The "New NPC" and "New Place" buttons in the NPCs & Places window make a ready page for you.

DNDAMIGOS.Help.Nethys.Title: Ask Nethys
DNDAMIGOS.Help.Nethys.Body: Rules questions without alt-tabbing. Nethys is the same rules helper as the Discord bot and the website's Ask Nethys page: it looks Pathfinder 2e Remaster and Starfinder 2e rules up on Archives of Nethys and links its source. Type /nethys followed by your question in the chat box for a private answer only you see, with a Share with table button. Use /nethys! to post the question and answer for everyone. Or open Ask Nethys from this menu for a small chat window you can keep beside the map; it remembers the conversation for follow-up questions until you start a new chat or close Foundry, and each answer has a Share to chat link. Nethys can still be wrong, so check the linked page for anything that matters.
DNDAMIGOS.Nethys.Placeholder: Ask about a rule, class, spell, condition…
DNDAMIGOS.Nethys.WindowHint: Enter to ask, Shift+Enter for a new line. In the chat box: /nethys <question> (private) or /nethys! <question> (everyone).
DNDAMIGOS.Nethys.Empty: Ask a rules question. Follow-ups remember the conversation.
DNDAMIGOS.Nethys.Usage: Type /nethys followed by your question, e.g. /nethys does grabbed make me off-guard? (Use /nethys! to answer for the whole table.)

Both open this same menu. If the & button is in your way, turn it off under Configure Settings → Show the D&D Amigos button (just for your browser).

DNDAMIGOS.Help.SessionSync.Title: End of Session Sync
DNDAMIGOS.Help.SessionSync.Body: One window that brings the website up to date at the end of a session, so the site is a current read-only record between games. It lists what will be sent, all ticked (untick anything you want to skip), then Sync sends each part and reports how it went. The GM's version sends the Party stash, every character in The Party (pushed to its Character Vault entry, or created there if it isn't linked yet), and NPCs & Places; the GM's identity must be the campaign's DM on the site. A player's version sends the Party stash and their own character. Characters and NPCs & Places need your identity set (My D&D Amigos Identity).

DNDAMIGOS.Setup.Title: D&D Amigos Connector — Setup Needed
DNDAMIGOS.Setup.Body:
This module isn't connected to the D&D Amigos website yet. To finish setup:

  1. On the website, an admin sets FOUNDRY_API_KEY and FOUNDRY_ORIGIN in engine/config.php (one time, for the whole group).
  2. Here, open Configure Settings → D&D Amigos Connection and fill in the Site URL, that same API Key, and the numeric Journal ID for this campaign (in the site's URL, e.g. journal.php?id=5 → 5).
  3. Click Test Connection to check it before saving.

Then every player (not just the GM) makes a personal token on their D&D Amigos Account page (Foundry Connection) and pastes it into Configure Settings → My D&D Amigos Identity once on each of their devices. That's how session posts, notes and character syncs know who they're from.

DNDAMIGOS.Settings.UserToken.Hint: From your D&D Amigos Account page → Foundry Connection. Saved in this browser only. Leave empty and Save to remove it.
DNDAMIGOS.Identity.Intro: Paste the personal token from your D&D Amigos Account page. The site uses it to know it's really you.

DNDAMIGOS.Identity.Cleared: Personal Foundry token removed from this browser.
DNDAMIGOS.Help.Recap.Title: Session Recap (GM)
DNDAMIGOS.Help.Recap.Body: Nethys drafts a session-log entry from tonight's chat as soon as you open it: there's nothing to fill in first. You get one preview, as the Session Log will show it. Most nights, read it and press Post. Edit turns it into one editable box; Rewrite takes an optional line (a fact Nethys missed, like "they found the vault key", or a style note like "shorter") and redraws the whole recap. The session is everything since the last recap; use change next to the time range if that's wrong. By the dice is counted exactly from the dice, never by the AI. Post adds it to the site's Session Log and this world's Session Recaps journal.
